question: Should OpenClaw expose live queue and workload state to agents through a new `queue_status` tool, and what visibility/redaction contract should that model-facing surface use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a public model-facing operational metadata contract that affects session visibility, queue safety limits, and related lane/capacity proposals.

options.title: Approve bounded queue_status
options.body: Add a read-only `queue_status` tool backed by a shared snapshot provider, with strict visibility filtering, profile/policy registration, docs, and tests.

options.title: Start with operator diagnostics
options.body: Keep the agent-facing issue open but first land a Gateway/CLI diagnostics surface and use that backend to settle metadata shape and redaction.

options.title: Fold into scheduler design
options.body: Pause this until the multi-lane and capacity proposals are designed together as one scheduling and observability contract.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded queue_status
recommendation.body: Add a read-only `queue_status` tool backed by a shared snapshot provider, with strict visibility filtering, profile/policy registration, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail runs through the current agent tool registry, `sessions_spawn`, tool catalog, and diagnostics surfaces this product/API choice would touch.
